service.name: Live music for an anniversary party
service.serviceType: A jazz duo, a singer with a guitar, a Spanish guitarist or a party band for 25th, 40th and 50th anniversary parties, surprise anniversary dinners and vow renewals
service.description: Live music for an anniversary party across Denver and the Front Range: a jazz duo playing the standards at 65 to 72 dBA under the dinner and the toasts, a singer with a guitar who learns the couple's first-dance song for the night, a Spanish guitarist for a long family dinner, and a trio or quartet for the anniversary that dances, at home, at a club or in a private dining space, with an announcement microphone for the toasts and one personal contact.

faqs.q: Can we hire a band for an anniversary party?
faqs.a: Yes. Most anniversaries are a seated dinner with a toast in it, so the jazz duo is the size to price first: upright bass and guitar playing the standards at 65 to 72 dBA at the nearest table. A singer with a guitar plays the anniversary where the couple's song has to be sung, and a trio or a quartet plays the 25th whose guests are still the people who danced at the wedding. It's one contract with one personal contact and an announcement microphone for the toasts.

faqs.q: Can the band play the couple's first-dance song?
faqs.a: Yes. The song from the wedding is learned for the night if it isn't already in the book, and the first learned song is included in every booking. Tell us the title with the date, and tell us whether it should be played or sung.

faqs.q: What are anniversary party entertainment ideas?
faqs.a: Their first-dance song played again while they dance in front of the people who watched the first time; a set built from the standards and the songs of the decade they met; a jazz duo under the dinner and silent for the toasts; a floor for the 25th; a Spanish guitarist under a long family dinner for the 50th; and live band karaoke for the wedding party, thirty years later.

faqs.q: How does a surprise anniversary party work with a musician?
faqs.a: The same way a proposal does. The musician is set up early and playing at conversation volume, so the place looks like it simply has live music that night, and the couple's song starts on a cue you and the musician agree beforehand, a nod from the host or a text from a friend at the next table. The proposals and surprise songs page covers the cue and the learned song in full.

faqs.q: Can you play a vow renewal and the dinner after it?
faqs.a: Yes, on one contract. A vow renewal in the garden books ceremony music, a guitarist or a duo for the walk in, the song the two of them chose and the walk out, and the same musicians play the dinner afterward at a volume the table talks across. The wedding ceremony page covers how ceremony music is placed.

faqs.q: What does live music for an anniversary party cost?
faqs.a: The pricing page sets out what live music costs in this market, and the cost guide has the Colorado figures for each kind of night. Send the date, the place and the couple's song and we'll come back with a configuration and a price for the night, with the vow renewal on the same quote if there is one.

faqs.q: How much space does the band need at a dinner?
faqs.a: A guitarist or a singer with a guitar takes 6 by 4 feet on one circuit, a duo 8 by 6 on one, a trio 12 by 8 on one and a quartet 14 by 10 on two, in the corner the table naturally faces. Load-in runs 45 minutes for a solo and an hour for a duo or a trio, and a restaurant's private dining space needs to know where the small case goes. Footprints for every size are on the technical page.
